final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the position to match the core limitation already identified in the initial audit. That clarification is useful, but it does not cure the unresolved compliance predicate. On the available record, aggregate readiness and rehearsal stability support a claim of operational readiness in general. They do not establish policy-complete certification for launch now, because the supplied policy makes the below-target segment material when it affects a named launch use case and legal review is pending. With no evidence of disclosure or approved risk acceptance, the caveat is not merely explanatory; it is the unresolved condition that blocks treating the certification claim as compliant, even with caveats.
remaining_concerns: The below-target public benefits eligibility segment is tied to named rollout commitments, which makes the weakness material under the supplied policy text.
No admissible evidence shows the issue was resolved, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Open legal review means the materiality question is not closed.

Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness but do not satisfy the separate policy predicate for a material weakness affecting a named launch use case.
The actor's narrowed framing is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new admissible evidence.
